newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end higher in moderate turnover.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end higher in moderate turnover.

text.p: After a slow start, Brazilian shares closed higher in speculative trade, led by bellwether Telebras, brokers said.
Telebras rose 2.55 percent to 141 reais, leading the Bovespa index of the 48 most active stocks to rise 1.83 percent to 10,691 points at the close.

Traders, who had expected very low volume due to holidays in the U.S. and Britain, were surprised by market turnover which totalled a moderate 455 million reais ($429.2 million), due mostly to local investors.
Among other blue-chips, federal power utility Eletrobras posted the highest gains, with a 1.17 percent rise to 519 reais.
State oil firm Petrobras rose 0.83 percent, while private CVRD rose 0.41 percent to 24.70 reais.
The voting stock of Minas Gerais state power firm Cemig jumped 4.35 percent to 48 reais ahead of the May 28 sale of a 32.9 percent stake in the firm, brokers said.
Rises in Cemig and Eletrobras stock contributed to a 2.49 percent rise in the power sector index, which comprises the nine most liquid stocks of the electrical industry.
